verdict.rationale: Twilio's Authy docs say it provides an official SDK for common web languages as an alternative to calling the Authy API directly. However, the same docs page now states the Authy API is closed to new customers and will be fully deprecated, with Verify v2 as the successor, so new builders effectively cannot adopt it. Missing for 10: availability to new integrators (deprecated and closed), the specific languages supported, SDK reference documentation, and hands-on or independent corroboration of SDK usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: So you don't have to use the Authy API directly to integrate two-factor authentication into your app, we provide an SDK for common web languages.
we provide an SDK for common web languages. If your language is supported, it's the fastest way to get started.
The Authy API is now closed to new customers and will be fully deprecated in the future.
